html: The Jingili, also written Jingulu, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory, around Newcastle Waters and the town of Elliott. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their language is not part of the Pama-Nyungan family that covers most of Australia. Their neighbours were the Mudburra to the west, the Alawa and Ngandi to the northeast and the Wambaya to the southeast. The Overland Telegraph Line passed through their country in 1872, and Newcastle Waters became a cattle station and a crossroads for drovers.
